statement: enforcer-memory's MCP/CLI surface (src/mcp.rs, src/cli.rs) wires 13 of 14 baseline tools to landed X06.1-X06.P1 library functions: index_repository, search_graph (bm25 only), query_graph, trace_path (calls mode only), get_code_snippet, get_graph_schema, get_architecture (full aspect set via architecture::build_report), search_code, list_projects/delete_project/index_status (crate::projects, over a caller-supplied storesDir registry), detect_changes, manage_adr. Only ingest_traces plus search_graph's regex/semantic modes and trace_path's data_flow/cross_service modes remain not_wired (owned by parallel lanes).
why: Salvaged a prior worker's uncommitted WIP from the dead worktree agent-ae662033c50b8e457, verified its module docs and dispatch pattern against the current, much-larger library surface, and extended wiring to 6 more tools (get_code_snippet, get_graph_schema, search_code, list_projects, delete_project, index_status) plus upgraded get_architecture from build_overview to the newer full-aspect build_report -- those library functions had landed since the salvage's older base commit.
howToApply: Any future tool/mode wiring is a one-line change in mcp.rs's dispatch_tool match arm (move from not_wired to a real handler) plus adding the name to WIRED_TOOLS. list_projects/delete_project/index_status take a storesDir param (crate::projects registry) rather than repoPath -- distinct from every other tool's stateless-rebuild-per-call pattern, since that is what their backing library functions actually persist.

statement: enforcer-memory's MCP server (src/mcp.rs) reuses enforcer-mcp::transport (FrameReader/encode_frame/RpcMessage/RpcResult/RpcError) directly rather than re-implementing dual Content-Length/NDJSON framing -- that module is pure I/O-free framing code with no business logic, so depending on it does not couple enforcer-memory to arc-21's tool surface, stdio sink, or stale-write gate. This required adding enforcer-mcp as a path dependency of enforcer-memory's Cargo.toml.
why: Avoids a second, drift-prone framing implementation; the wire contract (dual framing, Content-Length reply carries no trailing newline, NDJSON reply does) was independently verified against docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/refs/x06-baseline-tool-schemas.md and against enforcer-mcp's own transport.rs unit tests before reuse.
howToApply: Any crate wanting the same dual-framing JSON-RPC transport without pulling in arc-21's full tool registry should depend on enforcer-mcp and use only the transport module, following this exact pattern.

statement: During this lane's work, the concurrent x06-fed lane landed federation modules (artifacts.rs, share.rs, federation.rs, redaction.rs) into the same shared lib.rs/Cargo.toml this lane also needed to edit. The claim/release/intent protocol correctly serialized the edits (my claim->edit->release, their subsequent claim building on the released state) with no lost work; a transient build failure (missing redaction.rs, unresolved zstd/ed25519-dalek) was that lane's own in-flight work mid-landing, not a defect in this lane's edits, and resolved itself once their file landed.
why: Documents that the shared-file claim protocol worked as designed under real concurrent-lane contention, and that a transient red build during a shared-file window is not necessarily attributable to the most recent editor.
howToApply: When cargo build fails immediately after releasing a shared-file claim, check whether another lane's claim on the same paths is mid-flight before assuming your own edit broke the build -- re-run after a short wait / their completion notice.
